subject: Copywriting
title: The First Ads Were Carved in Stone
description: A micro-lesson that makes The First Ads Were Carved in Stone usable.

hook.text: In ancient Egypt, papyrus posters offered rewards for runaway slaves. Advertising started before paper.

buildup.text: Babylonian merchants carved sales pitches onto clay tablets. Roman walls had painted political slogans.

discovery.text: These early ads shared one trait: a clear promise. Buy this, come here, choose me. Simplicity worked.

twist.text: Pompeii's ruins revealed over 1,600 wall ads. Fast food shops, elections, gladiator fights—all promoted.

climax.text: The core formula hasn't changed in 3,000 years: grab attention, make a promise, ask for action.

punchline.text: 3,000 years of ads. The formula never changed.

quiz.question: Where were some of the earliest known advertisements found?
